subject.title: feat: per-job elevated exec scoping for cron and heartbeat

question: Should elevated cron and heartbeat authority be solved as narrow per-job/heartbeat approval markers, or folded into the broader non-forgeable scheduling and heartbeat provenance model?
rationale: The answer changes the host-elevated exec trust boundary across persisted cron jobs, agent-created schedules, HEARTBEAT.md/config edits, synthetic providers, and upgrade behavior, so automation should not choose the permanent model.

options.title: Fold Into Provenance Design
options.body: Treat this issue as the elevated-exec requirement for https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/71712 while explicitly keeping heartbeat provenance and migration in scope.

options.title: Implement Narrow Markers
options.body: Add per-job elevated approval state plus heartbeat modifier provenance now, with create/update/execution checks and upgrade tests.

options.title: Fail Closed Internals
options.body: Remove wildcard internal-source elevation for cron-event and heartbeat unless maintainers define an explicit compatibility path.

recommendation.title: Fold Into Provenance Design
recommendation.body: Treat this issue as the elevated-exec requirement for https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/71712 while explicitly keeping heartbeat provenance and migration in scope.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent merged cron caller-scope work makes joshavant the closest current routing owner for scheduling provenance decisions.
